senses.definition: The part that sticks out at the back of many animals’ bodies.
senses.example: The dog wagged its tail when we came home.

senses.definition: A long part that sticks out or trails behind something.
senses.example: Our kite had a tail made of ribbons.

senses.definition: To pick up or get something, or carry it with you to another place.
senses.example: I took my jacket when I left for school.

senses.definition: To need or use a particular amount of time, effort, or space.
senses.example: The walk took twenty minutes.

senses.definition: A story about something that happened or could have happened.
senses.example: We listened to a tale about a clever rabbit.

senses.definition: A small group of cells that helps you sense tastes.
senses.example: A taste bud can help send a message when sugar touches your tongue.

senses.definition: To help someone learn a fact, an idea, or a skill.
senses.example: My cousin taught me a new card game.

senses.definition: A little passage that takes tears from near an eye toward the nose.
senses.example: Tears can drain through a tear duct.

senses.definition: The thin coat of tears that covers the front of an open eye.
senses.example: Blinking spreads the tear film.

senses.definition: A large piece of Earth’s stiff outer layer. It moves very slowly compared with the other pieces.
senses.example: An earthquake can happen where two tectonic plates meet.

senses.definition: To give someone information or say what happened.
senses.example: I told my friend how we found the lost dog.

senses.definition: To notice or work out something by looking, listening, or thinking.
senses.example: I could tell the apple was ripe by how it smelled.

senses.definition: The speed of the beat in music.
senses.example: The dancers took quicker steps when the tempo got faster.

senses.definition: A strong strip of tissue that joins a muscle to a bone or another body part.
senses.example: A tendon carries the pull from your calf muscle to your heel bone.

senses.definition: A slender part of a climbing plant that can curl around something and hold on.
senses.example: A pea tendril curled around the string.

senses.definition: A flat, level area cut into a slope or built above the ground.
senses.example: The builders made a broad terrace for the palace.

senses.definition: Baked clay, often orange or reddish brown, used for pots, tiles, and figures.
senses.example: The artist shaped a terracotta figure from soft clay.

senses.definition: An area that someone controls or tries to keep.
senses.example: In Go, black surrounded territory along one side of the board.

senses.definition: An arrangement of shapes that can cover a flat surface without gaps or overlaps.
senses.example: Rows of matching square tiles made a tessellation.

senses.definition: A small piece used to build a mosaic.
senses.example: The red tessera helped fill the rim of the flower.

senses.definition: A material made by weaving, knitting, or otherwise joining threads or fibers.
senses.example: The textile had a rough surface and bright blue stripes.

senses.definition: A thin thread or strand that can be used to make cloth, paper or rope.
senses.example: The sweater was made with fibers from sheep’s wool.

senses.definition: To use your mind to consider something, form an idea, or solve a problem.
senses.example: We thought about where to look for the missing piece.

senses.definition: To believe or expect something without being completely sure.
senses.example: I think the bus will be here soon.

senses.definition: To send something through the air by swinging your arm and letting it go.
senses.example: I threw the beanbag toward the circle.

senses.definition: To arrange and give a party or other special event.
senses.example: We plan to throw a surprise party for Grandpa.

senses.definition: A push that moves a vehicle forward or in a chosen direction.
senses.example: Thrust from the propeller helped push the airplane forward.

senses.definition: A gland near the front of the neck that makes messages that help set how fast your body uses energy.
senses.example: The thyroid releases hormones into the blood.

senses.definition: A regular rise and fall of the ocean’s water level caused mostly by the pull of the Moon’s gravity. The Sun’s gravity also affects it.
senses.example: When the tide went out, we could see crabs in the rock pools.

senses.definition: A set of large bowl-shaped drums that can be tuned to specific notes.
senses.example: The player heard the timpani enter near the end.

senses.definition: Body material made of a group of cells and nearby material working together.
senses.example: Muscle tissue can pull as it shortens.

senses.definition: One of the hard parts in the mouth that help you bite and chew food.
senses.example: My loose tooth finally came out.

senses.definition: One of several little points that stick out in a row on something such as a comb or gear.
senses.example: A tooth broke off my comb.

senses.definition: A preserved sign of what a living thing did long ago, such as a track or burrow.
senses.example: The track in the rock is a trace fossil of a dinosaur walking.

senses.definition: To give something to someone and receive something else in return.
senses.example: I will trade a blue bead for a red one.

senses.definition: The buying, selling, or exchanging of goods and services.
senses.example: Trade brings some fruits from warm places to places where they cannot grow.

senses.definition: Work that uses a particular skill people can learn, such as fixing pipes or making furniture.
senses.example: It takes training and practice to learn the carpenter’s trade.

senses.definition: A feature of a living thing that can be noticed or measured.
senses.example: The color of a flower is a trait.

senses.definition: A device that uses a changing magnetic field between coils of wire to change electric voltage.
senses.example: The transformer lowers the voltage for use in the building.

senses.definition: The release of water vapor from a plant, mostly through its leaves.
senses.example: Transpiration added water vapor to the air around the tree.

senses.definition: A formal agreement between countries or other governments.
senses.example: The two countries signed a treaty to settle their disagreement about fishing rights.

senses.definition: A frame that a climbing plant can grow on.
senses.example: Pea plants climbed the trellis by the fence.

senses.definition: A flat shape with three straight sides and three corners.
senses.example: We cut a triangle from the corner of the paper.

senses.definition: A stream or river that flows into another stream or river.
senses.example: The creek is a tributary of the larger river downstream.

senses.definition: A muscle at the back of your upper arm that helps straighten your elbow.
senses.example: Your triceps muscle works when you push your hand away from your shoulder.

senses.definition: A chart that lists the result of a logic rule for each possible set of true and false choices.
senses.example: The truth table shows when the alarm button should turn on a sign.

senses.definition: A swollen part of a plant that stores food and can grow new shoots in some plants.
senses.example: A potato is a tuber on an underground stem.

senses.definition: A wheel with blades that spins when flowing water, air or steam pushes on it.
senses.example: Moving water turned a turbine inside the dam.

senses.definition: A long tooth that sticks out past an animal’s mouth.
senses.example: A narwhal’s tusk is a long tooth that sticks out from its upper jaw.

senses.definition: A way to sign in that checks two different kinds of proof that you are allowed to use the account.
senses.example: My family turned on two-factor authentication for an account.
